Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional People's Representative Council in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results or may result in suffering or distress of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other forms of violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.
19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to carry out their social functions normally in community life.

Article 13

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to:

a. implement the policy on Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence established by the Government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various non-governmental organizations concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
b. allocating budget for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity. (3) In the implementation of the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the implementation of the responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan for the protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence as referred to in Paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)

Point a

"Work network" means: family partners, dasawisma, family groups existing in the Region. Point b

Prevention efforts within the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening resilience in the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication between family members. Prevention efforts in the community include: fostering environmental awareness of acts of violence occurring in their environment.

Point c

"Violence prevention system" means: mapping of locations or areas prone to violence and conducting preventive efforts for the community.

Point d

Socialization can be carried out through mass media, electronic media, and direct outreach to the community. Point e

Critical education for women victims of violence is an effort to build women's awareness of their rights. The purpose of implementing critical education is to assist in decision-making and not to become victims of repeated violence. Forms of critical education for women victims of violence consist of: gender equality and justice training, education on reproductive health for women, and provision of understanding of laws and regulations on the Elimination of Domestic Violence.

Point f

Sufficiently clear.

Article 15

The community and family have the following obligations and responsibilities:

a. prevent the occurrence of violence against Women and Children; b. provide information and/or report acts of violence against Women and Children to law enforcement or authorized parties; c. participate in the handling of victims of acts of violence;
d. protect victims; and
e. provide emergency assistance.

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence. (2) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. coordination;

b. guidance;

c. education and training; and

d. monitoring and evaluation.

(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) are in order to realize the objectives of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) are carried out with professional and transparent principles.

(5) The Regional Apparatus is required to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of the Protection of Women Victims and Children involved in acts of violence.

Article 33

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Sambas Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state takes the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 12

(1) The Shelter House as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1) provides a place and/or temporary shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.

(2) The operation and/or management of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus. (3) For security and at the request of women victims of violence and children involved in acts of violence, the manager or operator of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) may place the person concerned in a specific confidential location.

(4) Further provisions regarding the operator of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 8

Other forms of violence as referred to in Article 2 letter f include:

a. any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's inherent freedom; and/or
b. a situation in which a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something against their own will.

Article 21

(1) Protection services for Women and Children from acts of violence may be carried out by UPTD PPA.

(2) As long as UPTD PPA has not been formed, the duties and functions of Protection services for Women and Children from acts of violence are carried out by the Regional Apparatus and related Institutions in an integrated and continuous manner.

(3) Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) may be delegated by UPTD PPA to other service units through networking and cooperation.

(4) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of a cooperation agreement.

Article 11

(1) In the event that women victims of acts of violence and children involved in acts of violence as referred to in Article 9 require continuous treatment, they are entitled to stay at a Shelter House or alternative residence.

(2) Continuous treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) is treatment at the rehabilitation stage carried out by individuals, groups or government and non-government institutions.

Article 22

Further provisions regarding the implementation of services for women victims and children involved in acts of violence as referred to in Article 19 are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "respect for and fulfillment of the rights of victims" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of the basic rights of victims.

Letter b

What is meant by "justice" is a situation where every person, both male and female, is treated equally and has equal opportunities to obtain access and welfare.

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in accessing employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d

What is meant by "the best interests of women and children" is all the best actions for women and children carried out by the Government, society, the legislative body and the judiciary, so that the best interests of women and children must be the primary consideration.

Letter e

What is meant by "empowerment" is the strengthening of women victims of violence so that they can work and earn a living independently after they have recovered and been provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

Article 3

Physical violence as referred to in Article 2 letter a is any form of act that results in:

a. the victim falling ill or seriously injured;
b. the death of the victim; and/or
c. causing illness or hindrance to carrying out work, occupation or livelihood or daily activities.

Article 5

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 2 letter c is in the form of: a. acts of sexual harassment;

b. forced sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or

c. forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.

18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.
19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to carry out their social functions normally in community life.

Article 33

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Sambas Regency.

Article 13

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to:

a. implement the policy on Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence established by the Government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various non-governmental organizations concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
b. allocating budget for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity. e. provide emergency assistance.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state takes the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional People's Representative Council in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results or may result in suffering or distress of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other forms of violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.
19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to carry out their social functions normally in community life.

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Sambas Regency.

CONCERNING

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state takes the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

a. any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's inherent freedom; and/or
b. a situation in which a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something against their own will.

Article 3

Physical violence as referred to in Article 2 letter a is any form of act that results in:

a. the victim falling ill or seriously injured;
b. the death of the victim; and/or
c. causing illness or hindrance to carrying out work, occupation or livelihood or daily activities.

Article 13

b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various non-governmental organizations concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
b. allocating budget for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity. (3) In the implementation of the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the implementation of the responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan for the protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence as referred to in Paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

Article 15

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state takes the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 13

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to:

a. implement the policy on Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence established by the Government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various non-governmental organizations concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
b. allocating budget for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity. (3) In the implementation of the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the implementation of the responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan for the protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence as referred to in Paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 12

(1) The Shelter House as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1) provides a place and/or temporary shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.

(2) The operation and/or management of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus. (3) For security and at the request of women victims of violence and children involved in acts of violence, the manager or operator of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) may place the person concerned in a specific confidential location.

(4) Further provisions regarding the operator of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional People's Representative Council in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results or may result in suffering or distress of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other forms of violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.
19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to carry out their social functions normally in community life.

Article 11

(1) In the event that women victims of acts of violence and children involved in acts of violence as referred to in Article 9 require continuous treatment, they are entitled to stay at a Shelter House or alternative residence.

(2) Continuous treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) is treatment at the rehabilitation stage carried out by individuals, groups or government and non-government institutions.

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence. (2) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. coordination;

b. guidance;

c. education and training; and

d. monitoring and evaluation.

(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) are in order to realize the objectives of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) are carried out with professional and transparent principles.

(5) The Regional Apparatus is required to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of the Protection of Women Victims and Children involved in acts of violence.

What is meant by "justice" is a situation where every person, both male and female, is treated equally and has equal opportunities to obtain access and welfare.

Article 12

(1) The Shelter House as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1) provides a place and/or temporary shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.

(2) The operation and/or management of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus. (3) For security and at the request of women victims of violence and children involved in acts of violence, the manager or operator of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) may place the person concerned in a specific confidential location.

Article 15

The community and family have the following obligations and responsibilities:

a. prevent the occurrence of violence against Women and Children; b. provide information and/or report acts of violence against Women and Children to law enforcement or authorized parties; c. participate in the handling of victims of acts of violence;

Letter a

Letter b

What is meant by "justice" is a situation where every person, both male and female, is treated equally and has equal opportunities to obtain access and welfare.

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in accessing employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state takes the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

Physical violence as referred to in Article 2 letter a is any form of act that results in:

a. the victim falling ill or seriously injured;
b. the death of the victim; and/or

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional People's Representative Council in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results or may result in suffering or distress of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other forms of violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.
19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to carry out their social functions normally in community life.

Paragraph (1)

Point a

Prevention efforts within the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening resilience in the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication between family members. Sufficiently clear.

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish A REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM VIOLENCE.

Article 15

The community and family have the following obligations and responsibilities:

a. prevent the occurrence of violence against Women and Children; b. provide information and/or report acts of violence against Women and Children to law enforcement or authorized parties; c. participate in the handling of victims of acts of violence;
d. protect victims; and
e. provide emergency assistance.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 22

Further provisions regarding the implementation of services for women victims and children involved in acts of violence as referred to in Article 19 are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 11

(1) In the event that women victims of acts of violence and children involved in acts of violence as referred to in Article 9 require continuous treatment, they are entitled to stay at a Shelter House or alternative residence.

(2) Continuous treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) is treatment at the rehabilitation stage carried out by individuals, groups or government and non-government institutions.

Article 12

(1) The Shelter House as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1) provides a place and/or temporary shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.

(2) The operation and/or management of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus. (3) For security and at the request of women victims of violence and children involved in acts of violence, the manager or operator of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) may place the person concerned in a specific confidential location.

(4) Further provisions regarding the operator of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)

Point a

"Work network" means: family partners, dasawisma, family groups existing in the Region. Point b

Prevention efforts within the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening resilience in the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication between family members. Prevention efforts in the community include: fostering environmental awareness of acts of violence occurring in their environment.

Point c

"Violence prevention system" means: mapping of locations or areas prone to violence and conducting preventive efforts for the community.

Point d

Socialization can be carried out through mass media, electronic media, and direct outreach to the community. Point e

Critical education for women victims of violence is an effort to build women's awareness of their rights. The purpose of implementing critical education is to assist in decision-making and not to become victims of repeated violence. Forms of critical education for women victims of violence consist of: gender equality and justice training, education on reproductive health for women, and provision of understanding of laws and regulations on the Elimination of Domestic Violence.

Point f

Sufficiently clear.

Article 29

Financing for the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "respect for and fulfillment of the rights of victims" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of the basic rights of victims.

Letter b

What is meant by "justice" is a situation where every person, both male and female, is treated equally and has equal opportunities to obtain access and welfare.

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in accessing employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d

What is meant by "the best interests of women and children" is all the best actions for women and children carried out by the Government, society, the legislative body and the judiciary, so that the best interests of women and children must be the primary consideration.

Letter e

What is meant by "empowerment" is the strengthening of women victims of violence so that they can work and earn a living independently after they have recovered and been provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional People's Representative Council in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results or may result in suffering or distress of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other forms of violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.
19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to carry out their social functions normally in community life.

NUMBER 2 OF 2022

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state takes the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state takes the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional People's Representative Council in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results or may result in suffering or distress of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other forms of violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.
19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to carry out their social functions normally in community life.

b. allocating budget for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity. (1) Implementation of empowerment as referred to in Article (24) and Article (25) is carried out by the Regional Apparatus and or related Institutions in an integrated and continuous manner.

(2) Further provisions regarding the implementation of empowerment as referred to in Paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional People's Representative Council in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results or may result in suffering or distress of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other forms of violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.
19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to carry out their social functions normally in community life.

Article 33

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Sambas Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state takes the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

CONCERNING

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

In order to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and prosecution of perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state takes the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not to do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children, whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect, do in fact occur, so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

The National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women states that Women as mothers of the nation and successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a proper and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional Governments also have an obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, Regional Governments require regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and prosecution of perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

a. prevent the occurrence of violence against Women and Children; b. provide information and/or report acts of violence against Women and Children to law enforcement or authorized parties; c. participate in the handling of victims of acts of violence;
d. protect victims; and
e. provide emergency assistance.

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence. (2) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. coordination;

b. guidance;

c. education and training; and

d. monitoring and evaluation.

(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) are in order to realize the objectives of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) are carried out with professional and transparent principles.

(5) The Regional Apparatus is required to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of the Protection of Women Victims and Children involved in acts of violence.

Article 13

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to:

a. implement the policy on Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence established by the Government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various non-governmental organizations concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
b. allocating budget for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity. (3) In the implementation of the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the implementation of the responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan for the protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence as referred to in Paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 33

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Sambas Regency.
